run_policy: Focused commands at most five minutes, provisioning ten; no production service, credentials, or destructive effect.

sources.text: Only entries dated within the range are listed, and each row's running balance continues from the opening balance.
With --since, the line after the heading is `Opening balance: <amount>`, the balance of every entry dated before --since.
Amounts are integer cents; never use floats for money. Every public function's docstring names the errors it raises.

candidates.title: Start row running balances from the opening balance
candidates.claim: With --since, statement_rows accumulates the running balance over every entry in posting order, so a row's running balance does not continue from the opening balance (sum of entries dated before --since) when entries are not posted in date order.
candidates.trigger: An account whose entries are not in date order (Ledger.post and the JSON loader accept any day) and --since is given, e.g. entries [2026-09-05 +5000, 2026-08-01 +1000, 2026-09-10 -200] with --since 2026-09-01.
candidates.impact: Opening balance prints 10.00 but the first row's running balance is 50.00 (should be 60.00) and the next 58.00 (should be 68.00); the statement is internally inconsistent, violating criterion 3.
candidates.change: In statement_rows, start running at balance_before(account, since) when since is given (and count only in-range entries), so each listed row continues from the opening balance.
